subject: sociology
title: Functionalism Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch your answers. Evaluate functionalism against Marxists, feminists and interactionists for full marks.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch evaluating functionalism with Marxist, feminist and interactionist critiques.
final_note: Top-band answers state, give a thinker, then offer a named critique.

concepts.def: When an institution stops doing its job properly.
Critique that functionalism backs the status quo.
Marxist label for functionalist claims of fairness.

walkthroughs.body_html: Marxists argue functionalists confuse the interests of capitalists with 'society's interests'. The 'value consensus' is really a ruling-class ideology that benefits owners, not workers.
Feminists like Oakley argue Parsons romanticised the nuclear family. The 'warm bath' was warm for men; for women it was a sink of unpaid housework. The 'expressive role' trapped women at home.
Interactionists say functionalism is too deterministic: people are not just puppets of roles. Becker showed labels and meanings matter in shaping behaviour.

mcqs.q: Merton's idea of a 'latent function' refers to:
Functionalism is often criticised for being:

options: All working-class people are an underclass.
A distinct group develops a culture of welfare dependency and anti-social behaviour.
Religion has completely disappeared from society.
Religion is becoming more important globally.
Religion is declining in social significance in modern societies.
The literal spread of McDonald's restaurants worldwide.
The spread of fast-food principles (efficiency, calculability, predictability, control) across society.
